candidateDecisions.label: A clinical-psychology and mental-health direction centred on stress, trauma, psychological disorders, health and clinical science.
candidateDecisions.reason: The broad plan already contains psychopathology, assessment and psychotherapy, health psychology and development. The current options do not sustain a separate plan with materially deeper clinical methods and supervised practice.

candidateDecisions.label: A developmental-psychology direction centred on children, identity and development across the lifespan.
candidateDecisions.reason: Lifespan development, health and youth resilience fit within the broad plan. The active curriculum lacks enough distinct developmental and child-assessment study to sustain a separate direction at comparable depth.

analysis: The broad plan retains the full psychology sequence across brain, social psychology, development, psychopathology, assessment and health, and uses quantitative, qualitative and evidence-synthesis methods. Sociology and behavioral economics complement psychological work with institutions and decisions. The brain and cognition plan combines neurobiology, perception, psycholinguistics and higher cognition with physiology, laboratory practice, philosophy of mind and emotion, Python and data methods. Programming and statistics prepare for later computational work. Computer vision teaches image representations and machine vision, which complement study of human perception without supplying neuroscience. The work plan combines social psychology, leadership, stress, negotiation, diversity and behavioral choice with market and qualitative research. AI in business and international governance address organizational context, not core psychology. Clinical and developmental topics already have a credible home in the broad plan. The alternatives cannot support clinical training or a developmental direction at substantially greater depth. Eight positive alignments document shared subject matter or methods. Utrecht’s advanced statistics, interviewing, specialized clinical theory and required research remain distinguishable from UCR coursework.

alignment.rationale: Both study social cognition, attitudes and group behavior.
Both study cognitive, social and emotional development across the lifespan.
Utrecht examines psychology as a scientific discipline. UCR develops scientific reasoning across several courses.
Both introduce brain function and the links between biology and behavior.
Both examine psychological disorders and their explanations.
Both examine attention and memory. The UCR course approaches these functions through neuroscience.
Utrecht offers dedicated clinical theory. UCR studies related topics in psychopathology and health psychology.
Utrecht studies cognitive changes in clinical settings. UCR focuses on mechanisms of perception and cognition.
Utrecht focuses on clinical questions in child development. UCR studies development across the lifespan.
Both use research designs and statistical inference to answer psychological questions.
Utrecht develops advanced statistical analysis. UCR’s advanced psychology methods course focuses on systematic reviews and meta-analysis.
Both introduce research design, measurement and statistical inference.
Both introduce Python programming. Utrecht’s training uses examples from psychology.
This course examines motivation and self-regulation in everyday life.
This course examines how contemporary technologies affect behavior and well-being.
Utrecht offers dedicated practice in developing and running experiments. UCR studies experimental design alongside statistics.
Utrecht requires a supervised 15 EC research project. UCR’s optional independent research is shown separately.
Utrecht provides structured practice in psychological interviewing. UCR studies communication and assessment across several courses.
